title: Sections commute with homology for section-acyclic terms and homology
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme, $K^\bullet$ a nonnegative cochain complex of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $V\subseteq Y$ an open. Assume $H^r(V,K^n|_V)=0$ and $H^r(V,\mathcal H^n(K)|_V)=0$ for every $n\geq0$ and $r>0$, where cohomology is module right-derived sections [pqf-def-cohomology]. Then the canonical map $H^p(K^\bullet(V))\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal H^p(K))$ sending a section cocycle to its sheaf homology class is an isomorphism for every $p\geq0$. In the prescribed model it is evaluation at $V$ of sectionCohomologyTheta [def-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-open-choices], with its source identified by exact homology evaluation. No affineness, quasi-coherence, morphism of schemes, or resolution comparison is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 015J, both Cartan--Eilenberg spectral sequences and their finite convergent filtrations; Tag 01E4 for the cocycle normalization

proof.text: Restrict the nonnegative complex K to V. Restriction is exact, so its homology is the restriction of the homology of K. Form a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution. The first hypercohomology spectral sequence has E1 terms H^r(V,K^n|V); the term-vanishing hypothesis kills rows r>0, so its abutment is H^p(K(V)).

The second hypercohomology spectral sequence has E2 terms H^r(V,H^n(K)|V). The homology-vanishing hypothesis kills columns r>0. Thus the same abutment is Gamma(V,H^p(K)). Nonnegative support gives finite filtrations in each total degree, so both edge comparisons are isomorphisms.

The composite edge sends a section cocycle to its image under the homology projection. The augmentation of the double resolution preserves that representative. Exact sheafification and its counit identify this cocycle map with sectionCohomologyTheta; exact evaluation identifies its presheaf-homology source with H^p(K(V)). Therefore theta evaluated at V is an isomorphism. Degree zero uses the kernel and augmentation; for empty V all sections are zero.

proof_origin.place: Specialization of both spectral sequences to section-acyclic terms and homology, with explicit cocycle identification
